SIGIL SARL — Buea, Cameroon

Cybersecurity in Buea

The honest answer, in two parts

Ask about cybersecurity in Buea and you will mostly hear about training — and the training is real. The town on the slopes of Mount Cameroon hosts a university that teaches cryptosystems to master's level, an active OWASP chapter, and the developer community that calls itself Silicon Mountain. That is the first part of the answer, and Buea has earned it.

The second part is a gap. A region that produces security talent in numbers still has very little commercial practice built to the standard public institutions actually need: engagements that are authorized before they are technical, findings that are re-verified before they are reported, and evidence that survives an auditor. This page lays out both parts, and states plainly what SIGIL SARL, a company registered in Buea (RCCM RC.BUA.2026.B.0190), is building to close the second.

The talent pipeline on the mountain

The Department of Computer Engineering at the University of Buea's Faculty of Engineering and Technology runs the region's most formal security pipeline: a B.Eng in Computer Engineering, an M.Eng in Cryptosystems and Cyber Security, and a Ph.D programme in Network Security and Distributed Systems. Security is not incidental coverage there; it is taught as a named discipline, from undergraduate network engineering through doctoral research.

Alongside the university sits the OWASP Buea chapter, established in 2024 under the OWASP Foundation to promote secure software development in the local tech community. The chapter runs workshops, meetups, and hackathons open to anyone, and collaborates with the University of Buea Cybersecurity Club on events that mix OWASP Top 10 demonstrations with capture-the-flag competitions and penetration-testing challenges.

Both draw on the broader ecosystem known as Silicon Mountain — the community of startups, developers, and hubs that has grown in Buea since the early 2010s. ActivSpaces, launched in 2009, is among the country's earliest tech hubs; Google Developer Group Buea has helped grow the ecosystem since 2013; and the community kept building through the internet shutdowns that disrupted Cameroon's anglophone regions in 2017. Talent, in short, is not Buea's problem.

Cybersecurity in Buea: the gap the pipeline does not fill

Here is what the training pipeline does not produce on its own: governance-grade practice. A graduate of the mountain can find a vulnerability. An institution — a ministry, a regulator, a university administration, a public agency — needs something harder: the vulnerability found under written authorization, confirmed by an independent check, remediated, and documented in evidence that will still stand when an auditor reads it a year later. Those are different trades, and the second is scarce in Buea, as it is in most of the region.

The obligations, meanwhile, already exist. Cameroon's Law No. 2010/012 of 21 December 2010 governs the security of electronic communication networks and information systems and defines the offences committed against them, and ANTIC, the National Agency for Information and Communication Technologies, is mandated under Article 7 of that law to carry out technology watch and issue alerts and recommendations on network security, and operates a national Computer Incident Response Team. An institution engaging any security partner in Buea is operating inside that framework, and should choose a partner that treats it as a floor rather than a ceiling.

Naming this gap is not a criticism of the training ecosystem — the pipeline is the precondition for everything else. It is a statement about what remains to be built on top of it.

What SIGIL builds from Buea

SIGIL SARL was founded in 2023 in Buea by Junior Thuram Nana and builds sovereign governance infrastructure for public institutions. Three systems are in development: VIGIL, a governed cybersecurity and evidence platform; RÉCOR, a sovereign beneficial-ownership registry designed for Cameroon; and APEX, anti-corruption intelligence for public procurement. All three are pre-deployment, and all source code is kept strictly private.

VIGIL is the system this page concerns. It is designed to help duly authorized operators find, confirm, remediate, and document vulnerabilities under one rule: a technical capability is never an authorization. No model or agent can authorize itself, and no finding is trusted until an independent, re-verifiable check confirms it. The full argument for why security tooling should be governed this way is set out on our governed cybersecurity page; the doctrine beneath it fits in one sentence: the institution holds the keys; the data stays under the institution's control; every consequential action is authorized, bounded, and proven.

And the honesty owed to the reader: we are a young company. SIGIL has no customers, no deployments, no pilots, and no revenue to point to. What we offer instead is precision about what we are building and how it can be verified — every claim on this site is written so an evaluator can test it against the system in front of them. Our wider position in Cameroon's public-sector technology landscape is set out on the govtech hub.

What to demand of any security partner

These six criteria are derived from our doctrine, but they are not about us: they are what any institution in the region should put in writing before engaging any security partner — SIGIL included. An evaluator should hold VIGIL to every line of this table.

DemandWhy it matters
Written, bounded authorization before any testA capability is never an authorization. The scope of an engagement should be fixed in writing before a single packet is sent — and anything outside it refused by the partner's own tooling, not merely by their good manners.
Independent re-verification of every findingA scanner's output is a lead, not a fact. Reports should separate what an independent, deterministic check has confirmed from what was merely observed — and never present the absence of a signal as proof of absence.
Key and data custody with your institutionNo vendor default access, no hidden administrative account, no operational telemetry leaving your infrastructure. If custody sits with the partner, so does the power.
The standing right to read, export, and stopWhatever the state of the contract or licence, your institution should always be able to read and export its own data and trip a safe stop. A partner who cannot grant this in writing is asking for trust instead of offering proof.
Tamper-evident evidence and signed reportsEvery consequential action of an engagement should be attributable in an audit trail that cannot be quietly rewritten, and final reports should be signed and re-checkable offline.
A written legal basis under Cameroonian lawSecurity testing in Cameroon operates inside the framework of Law No. 2010/012 of 21 December 2010. A serious partner states the legal basis of each engagement in writing, alongside the authorization.

Frequently asked

Are there cybersecurity companies in Buea?

Buea's security reputation rests mostly on training and community: the University of Buea teaches cybersecurity to master's and doctoral level, and an OWASP chapter has run workshops and capture-the-flag events since 2024. Commercial security firms are far scarcer. SIGIL SARL, registered in Buea under RCCM RC.BUA.2026.B.0190, is one: it is building VIGIL, a governed cybersecurity and evidence platform. VIGIL is pre-deployment, and SIGIL currently has no customers or deployments — a fact we state plainly rather than around.

Can SIGIL run a security engagement for my institution today?

Not today. VIGIL is pre-deployment: SIGIL has no customers, deployments, or pilots, and we do not sell what we cannot yet govern to our own standard. What an institution can do now is examine the doctrine VIGIL is built to, test the claims on this site, and hold us — and every other prospective partner — to the six criteria on this page. Questions reach us at info@sigilsovereign.com.

Where can I learn cybersecurity in Buea?

The University of Buea's Faculty of Engineering and Technology offers a B.Eng in Computer Engineering, an M.Eng in Cryptosystems and Cyber Security, and a Ph.D in Network Security and Distributed Systems. Outside the university, the OWASP Buea chapter runs free workshops, meetups, and hackathons, and Silicon Mountain community hubs such as ActivSpaces have hosted developer training in Buea for over a decade.
